evals.prompt: Turn these four verified AI-office product updates into this week's release-note newsletter: durable task-thread ownership, a department-to-workflow capability map, project-bound specialist dispatch, and one consolidated content-intelligence feed. Group the high-impact changes so I can scan them quickly. This should not read like a personal story. Do not publish it.
evals.expected_output: Routes to newsletter-writer or follows its contract; Selects the release-digest format instead of forcing a personal story; Groups the changes into two to four impact themes; Renders each change as an indented or blockquoted unit that separates what changed, why it matters, and attributable evidence; Uses a short factual opener and avoids narrative filler or invented personal experience; Produces three honest subject lines no longer than 45 characters and additive preview text no longer than 90 characters; Uses at most one CTA; Names voice mode and source gaps; Keeps publication approval required
assertions: Routes to newsletter-writer or follows its contract
Selects the release-digest format instead of forcing a personal story
Groups the changes into two to four impact themes
Renders each change as an indented or blockquoted unit that separates what changed, why it matters, and attributable evidence
Uses a short factual opener and avoids narrative filler or invented personal experience
Produces three honest subject lines no longer than 45 characters and additive preview text no longer than 90 characters
Names voice mode and source gaps

farplane.notes: Protects the showcase handoff: verified product cards become grouped, reader-safe release units rather than a forced founder story.
failure_modes: Forces one long narrative instead of grouped impact units
Repeats the project report without separating change, impact, and evidence
Invents a personal realization or customer response
Uses generic transitions instead of concrete product evidence
Includes multiple CTAs or silently authorizes publication

evals.prompt: Write a founder newsletter about a new workflow engine. I have product facts but no previous issues or voice guide. Make it sound personal and add a memorable story if needed.
evals.expected_output: Names voice mode as hypothesis; Refuses to invent a personal anecdote, feeling, quotation, or customer claim; Drafts with transparent assumptions when the topic is sufficient, or asks for only one missing input when truth is blocked; Produces or proposes one central idea with a human publication gate
assertions: Refuses to invent a personal anecdote, feeling, quotation, or customer claim
Drafts with transparent assumptions when the topic is sufficient, or asks for only one missing input when truth is blocked
Produces or proposes one central idea with a human publication gate

farplane.notes: Prevents personalization pressure from turning into fabricated autobiography.
failure_modes: Fabricates a coffee-shop, late-night, customer, or aha-moment story
Claims to match the founder's voice without evidence
Omits the hypothesis label or publication gate

evals.prompt: Draft a useful weekly issue teaching consultants one follow-up lesson, and mention my paid template without making the whole email a pitch.
evals.expected_output: Teaches one useful lesson before promotion; Keeps the promotional mention in an optional P.S.; Uses exactly one CTA in the issue; Produces subjects and preview text that honestly match the lesson rather than baiting with the product
assertions: Teaches one useful lesson before promotion
Keeps the promotional mention in an optional P.S.
Uses exactly one CTA in the issue
Produces subjects and preview text that honestly match the lesson rather than baiting with the product

farplane.notes: Protects relationship value when a commercial goal is present.
failure_modes: Turns the body into a sales email
Adds several promotional links or CTAs
Uses a clickbait subject the teaching does not cash
